commits.edited_message:
don't preallocate vectors when parsing IDManifests (#2575)

* don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests

Build the _manifest list incrementally instead of resizing it up front
to an entry count taken straight from the file, so a bogus count can no
longer force a large speculative allocation before any entry is read.

* build the string-index mapping table in place too

The mapping table is populated one entry at a time as the run-length
blocks are decoded, so there is no need to preallocate it to the string
count either. Build it with push_back as each referenced index is seen,
and bound the per-ID string references against the mapping that actually
backs them (mapping.size()) rather than the raw string list.

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>
Co-authored-by: Maintainer H <maintainer-h@example.invalid>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bound IDManifest uncompressed size, version field, and string references (#2572)

A single unvalidated 64-bit `_uncompressedDataSize` field, read directly
from an EXR file's `idManifest` attribute, was used as a `std::vector`
allocation size in `IDManifest::IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)`
before decompression and before any consistency check. Depending on the
value an attacker writes into that field, an application that reads ID
manifests can be forced to either exhaust memory (an uncatchable SIGKILL,
since the vector's value-initialization physically dirties every page)
or dereference a null pointer, because a declared size of 0 makes
`uncomp.data()` null while the length check that follows decompression
still passes (0 == 0). Declared sizes of 1-3 instead produce a silent
heap out-of-bounds read of the version field. All of this is reachable
from a 343-byte file through the public, non-explicit, IMF_EXPORT
constructors `IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)` and
`IDManifest(const char*, const char*)`.

Three checks are added:

- In the `CompressedIDManifest` constructor, reject the declared
  uncompressed size before allocating anything for it if it is zero, or
  exceeds the compressed size scaled by zlib's maximum expansion ratio
  (~1032:1) -- tying the claim to bytes that must actually be present in
  the file, rather than trusting an arbitrary 64-bit value. This does
  *not* impose an absolute size ceiling: OpenEXR places no fixed limit
  on data size by default (see `Header::setMaxImageSize()`, which is
  off/unlimited unless an application opts in), so a legitimate manifest
  may be arbitrarily large provided the file actually contains that much
  compressed data.

- In `IDManifest::init()`, bounds-check the 4-byte version field read
  against the end of the buffer, exactly as the adjacent
  `readStringList()` already does for its own reads. This is the fix
  that actually matters for the null/overread cases, since `init()` is
  reachable directly through the public `IDManifest(const char*, const
  char*)` constructor without ever passing through the size check above.

- Still in `init()`, validate each decoded per-ID string reference
  against the size of the string list it selects from, so that a
  reference decoded from the file can only ever name a string that is
  actually present in the manifest's string table.

Also replaced `&uncomp[0]` with `uncomp.data()`, which is well-defined
for an empty vector.

Addresses https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr/security/advisories/GHSA-5j5m-22wr-mhc6

Signed-off-by: Maintainer H <maintainer-h@example.invalid>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+    // Reject an implausible declared uncompressed size before allocating
+    // anything for it. The declared size is otherwise an unvalidated
+    // 64-bit value taken directly from the file, used as a buffer size
+    // before decompression (and thus before any check on its contents),
+    // which allows a tiny file to force an enormous, fully-committed

coupling:
Delocalized heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) in IDManifest::init() (src/lib/OpenEXR/ImfIDManifest.cpp), reachable through the public IMF_EXPORT constructor Imf::IDManifest(const char* data, const char* end).

The read at `stringList[mapping[stringIndex]]` needs TWO facts to be safe: (a) `stringIndex < mapping.size()` so the `mapping[]` access is in bounds, and (b) the stored mapping value is a valid stringList index. In the base code these were coupled implicitly: `mapping` was preallocated to `stringList.size()` (`vector<int> mapping (stringList.size())`) and value-initialized, so the single bound check `stringIndex < stringList.size()` simultaneously guarded the `mapping[]` access (because mapping.size()==stringList.size()) and any unmapped slot read a harmless 0.

Commit d6f75dc ('don't preallocate vectors when parsing IDManifests') legitimately stops preallocating: it builds `mapping` incrementally with push_back, so mapping.size() now equals the number of distinct string indices the run-length block actually references, which can be strictly less than stringList.size(). To stay correct, that same commit tightens the per-ID reference check to `stringIndex < mapping.size()` -- the container actually being indexed. Read on its own this commit is correct and safe (a reference past the mapping is rejected with InputExc, see the d6f75dc-only intermediate).

Commit 38d9cbf ('Bound IDManifest uncompressed size, version field, and string references') changes the same per-ID reference check to validate against `stringList.size()` -- framed as bounding the reference against the string list it ultimately selects from. Read on its own (i.e. applied without d6f75dc, where mapping is still preallocated to stringList.size()) this is an identity: mapping.size()==stringList.size(), so it changes nothing and the tree stays safe (see the 38d9cbf-only intermediate).

Only the COMPOSITION is unsafe: after both commits, `mapping` is incrementally sized (<= stringList.size()) while the surviving bound check uses stringList.size(), so a crafted manifest whose run-length block references fewer string indices than exist in the string list, and whose ID table then names a string index in [mapping.size(), stringList.size()), passes the check and reads `mapping[stringIndex]` past the end of the heap buffer.

Why a correct fix is non-local: fixing d6f75dc's diff in isolation finds nothing wrong -- its bound (mapping.size()) matches its own incremental mapping. Fixing 38d9cbf's diff in isolation also finds nothing wrong -- bounding a string reference by the string-list size is the obviously-correct intent, and is a no-op on the preallocated mapping that commit sees in isolation. A real fix requires reasoning across both commits: recognizing that d6f75dc made mapping.size() diverge from stringList.size() and that 38d9cbf's bound must therefore track mapping, not the string list.

pocs.entry_point: Imf::IDManifest(const char* data, const char* end) public IMF_EXPORT constructor (<ImfIDManifest.h>)
